content.topic: Management of patients with heart failure before and during pregnancy

anticoagulation_recommendations.summary: Therapeutic anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) is recommended in the first and last trimesters; vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with usual target INRs or LMWH in the second trimester is recommended for patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF). Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) should be avoided.

assessment_recommendations: Clinical assessment including symptoms, clinical examination, blood pressure (BP), oxygen saturation (SaO2), ECG and resting echocardiography for patients with HF in pre-pregnancy or at presentation with a new pregnancy.
Modalities of delivery should be planned by cardiologists, obstetricians, and anaesthesiologists around 35 weeks in a multidisciplinary Pregnancy Heart Team.

follow_up_and_monitoring.bimonthly_or_monthly: Bimonthly assessments for women in mWHO IIa/IIb/III, and monthly assessments for women with pre-existing HF in mWHO III.
follow_up_and_monitoring.reassessment_timing: Reassessment at the beginning of the second trimester (around 20 weeks) and reassessment at 20 weeks as noted in pathway.

referral_and_counselling: Women with advanced HF (LVEF <30%, NYHA class III–IV) in mWHO IV who are pregnant can be referred to a specialist centre for counselling regarding any consideration of termination of pregnancy.
Referral to a specialist centre with a multidisciplinary Pregnancy Heart Team for moderate and high-risk HF patients (mWHO II, III and IV).
Low-risk HF patients (mWHO I) should still be discussed with a specialist centre for high-risk pregnancies as appropriate.
content.therapy_review: Review HF therapy at diagnosis/planning and switch to non-teratogenic HF medication where indicated.
content.figure_description: Flowchart (Figure 19) showing management pathway before and during pregnancy: pre-pregnancy counselling, cardiac assessment at pregnancy diagnosis/planning, review of HF therapy, stratification into moderate/high-risk (mWHO II–IV) versus low-risk (mWHO I) with associated referral, reassessment at ~20 weeks, and ongoing review frequency (bimonthly/monthly) and urgent counselling for pregnancy termination consideration for mWHO IV.
